name: fix_fastapi_password_leak
description: Fixes a list endpoint leaking password_hash by enforcing the public schema
prompts: The GET /users list endpoint in app/routers/users.py leaks sensitive data: it has no response_model, so it serializes the raw repository dicts - which include password_hash - straight to clients. Fix the leak so NO endpoint ever returns password_hash (or any password field). Apply the public UserOut schema to the list endpoint (response_model=list[UserOut]); if you need a list-output type, add it to app/schemas.py. The list must still return every user's id, username, and email. POST /users and GET /users/{id} keep working and must also never leak the hash.

setup_files.app/schemas.py:
from pydantic import BaseModel


class UserCreate(BaseModel):
    username: str
    email: str
    password: str


class UserOut(BaseModel):
    id: int
    username: str
    email: str
setup_files.app/main.py:
from fastapi import FastAPI

from app.routers import users

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(users.router)

test_setup_files.test_leak.py:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

client.post("/users", json={"username": "ada", "email": "a@x.io", "password": "s3cret"})
client.post("/users", json={"username": "bob", "email": "b@x.io", "password": "hunter2"})

r = client.get("/users")
assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
users = r.json()
assert len(users) == 2, users
for u in users:
    assert "password_hash" not in u, f"password_hash leaked in list: {u}"
    assert "password" not in u, f"password leaked in list: {u}"
    assert set(u.keys()) == {"id", "username", "email"}, f"unexpected fields: {u}"
assert {u["username"] for u in users} == {"ada", "bob"}

# single-user endpoint must also stay clean
r = client.get("/users/1")
assert "password_hash" not in r.json(), r.json()
print("PASS")
